newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer positive on settlement risk progress.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer positive on settlement risk progress.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Monday he saw progress in tackling the settlement risks in the foreign exchange system and described recent initiatives as positive.

Speaking to reporters in his capacity as chairman of the Group of 10 (G-10 ) central bank governors committee, Tietmeyer said William McDonough, president of the New York Federal Reserve, had delivered an interim report to the governors on foreign exchange settlement risks.
"It shows there is real progress under way and that banks are really increasingly aware of settlement risks and a lot of initiatives are starting," Tietmeyer said.
The G-10 last year launched a wide-ranging strategy to tackle the risk of a break-down in the settlement of foreign exchange deals.
The key point of the strategy was that private banks should improve their settlement systems.
McDonough, Chairman of the Bank for International Settlement's committee on payments and settlement systems, gave the governors an interim report.
Tietmeyer said he hoped a final report would be finished by the end of this year.

The Group of 20, a group of the world's leading commercial banks, recently decided to create a London-based company that would set up a bank to settle foreign exchange deals based on the principle of a Continuous Linked Settlements (CLS).
